entries.title: Rain
entries.text:
Rain

hazefogsmokedustsnowsteam

Rain in film is falling water that makes air visible as streaks and turns the ground into a mirror. Drops are matter in the optical path; without backlight they vanish, and without a wet-down the street stays dry under a fake storm.

Create this Rain

Narrative function

Silver needles between a lamp and the lens. Shoulders darken.

Puddles double the neon. Weather is percussion you can see.

Make the air visible and the ground reflective. Use it when the scene must be wet in depth, not only on a window pane.

It is the wrong tool when you only need specular streets at night with no falling drops: that is a Wet-Down. It is also the wrong tool when you want a still veil that hides geography: that is Fog.

Rain against a bright overcast sky reads as nothing. Put a light behind the drops, toward camera, or lose the storm.

How it works

Put water in the air (rain bars, towers, or a real front) and light it from behind or the side so droplets scatter toward the lens. Keep a darkish background so streaks separate.

Wet the ground even if the rain is light. Shutter angle controls streak length versus beads.

Prompt: heavy rain around [Subject], backlit drops, wet-down pavement, umbrellas, silver streaks, weather as percussion.

When to use it

Use it for a night street, a rooftop, a prison yard, any beat that needs falling water as a layer. Do not use it as a grade or as window tracks only.

If the air is empty and the asphalt is merely shiny, you shot a wet-down.

Compared with similar shots

A Wet-Down soaks surfaces so lights double; it need not rain. Atmospheric Haze is a distant scatter, not falling drops.

Snow is ice that settles and accumulates. Fog is a local veil that hides figures.

Rain falls, streaks when backlit, and leaves the ground wet.

Wet-DownNight exteriors that must sparkle.

Atmospheric HazeShow kilometers, not just meters.

FogHide geography. Delay the reveal.

In film

Blade Runner builds night as backlit rain and reflective streets. Seven uses rain as a constant layer over investigation.

The Shawshank Redemption lets a yard storm become a body-length release. Use drop, backlight, and wet ground, not a copied coat.

Prompt it

Heavy rain around [Subject], backlit drops, wet-down pavement, umbrellas, silver streaks, weather as percussion. Name the backlight (a streetlamp, a sign, a HMI behind the rain), the wet ground, and drop size.

For video, falling streaks in depth, splashes, no dry asphalt. Do not write a mood word in place of the water.

Use in Image Generator

Heavy cinematic rain around [Subject], backlit drops, wet-down pavement, umbrellas, silver streaks, weather as percussion.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Wet-Down (shiny street, empty air) or a blue LUT called rain. The tell: no streaks against lamps, dry shoulders, no puddles.

The fix: put drops in the air, backlight them, wet the ground.

Questions

What is Rain in film?

Rain is falling water used as visible matter: backlit streaks in the air and reflective ground. Both the optical path and the pavement have to be wet.

Rain vs Wet-Down

A wet-down sprays surfaces so night lights specularize, often with no weather in the air. Rain adds falling drops. You usually wet-down under rain; you can wet-down without rain.

When should I use Rain?

Use it when air must streak and ground must mirror. Do not use it if you only need a shiny street, and do not expect rain to read against a bright empty sky without backlight.

How do I prompt Rain for AI image or video?

Name backlit drops and wet ground. Example: heavy rain around [Subject], backlit drops, wet-down pavement, silver streaks. Specify the lamp behind the rain and forbid dry asphalt.

entries.title: Fog
entries.text:
Fog

hazesmokedustrainsnowsteam

Fog is a dense local suspension of water droplets that collapses depth, turns lamps into globes, and delays the reveal of figures. The air is matter close to camera; geography hides until someone walks into the last few meters.

Create this Fog

Narrative function

A sodium lamp becomes a ball. A platform ends in nothing.

A coat arrives late, as if the world were only as large as a flashlight. Hide geography.

Delay the reveal. Use it for horror, docks, London streets, any beat that should withhold the next plane.

It is the wrong tool when you still want kilometers of readable landscape: that is Atmospheric Haze. It is the wrong tool when the veil is thin and lyrical: that is Mist.

Combustion with a source is Smoke. If faces at three meters are crisp and only the grade is grey, you do not have fog.

You have a LUT.

How it works

Fill a volume with dense droplets (machines or weather) so contrast falls with distance on a short scale. Backlight or sidelight the fog to make globes around practicals; front light flattens it to milk.

Keep practicals inside the soup, not only a filter on the lens. Prompt: dense fog around [Subject], depth collapsing, lamps becoming globes, figures appearing late, horror or London grammar.

When to use it

Use it when a figure should appear late, a road should end in white, a house should have no yard. Do not use it on a vista you still need to read.

If the far ridge must stay a ridge, use haze or mist.

Compared with similar shots

Mist is thinner: layered, see-through, lyric. Atmospheric Haze stacks paler planes over kilometers, not a wall at ten meters.

Smoke has a source and a direction and is not weather. Steam rises from heat and thins as it cools.

Fog is a local, dense water veil.

MistSofter mystery than fog. Lyric, not monster.

Atmospheric HazeShow kilometers, not just meters.

RainMake the air visible and the ground reflective.

In film

The Exorcist and The Others use fog to withhold houses, lamps, and bodies. Sicario lets dust and fog-like veils erase desert edges (a cousin in opacity).

Use delayed reveal and globes around lamps, not a copied graveyard.

Prompt it

Dense fog around [Subject], depth collapsing, lamps becoming globes, figures appearing late. Name density (visibility in meters), the practicals blooming, and what is hidden.

For video, figures emerging from soup, no crisp far architecture. Do not describe a grey grade on a clear street.

Use in Image Generator

Dense fog around [Subject], depth collapsing, lamps becoming globes, figures appearing late, horror or London grammar.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Atmospheric Haze (distance) or a desaturated grade. The tell: sharp buildings a block away, lamps with no globes, faces fully lit at thirty meters.

The fix: short visibility, backlit bloom on lights, late arrivals.

Questions

What is Fog in film?

Fog is a dense local cloud of water droplets that hides depth. Lamps bloom into globes and figures appear only when they enter the near ground.

Fog vs Mist

Fog is opaque enough to collapse geography at short range. Mist is thinner, layered, and still lets you read the next plane. Fog withholds; mist veils.

When should I use Fog?

Use it to hide geography and delay a reveal. Do not use it when you need a long, readable landscape, and do not fake it with a grey LUT.

How do I prompt Fog for AI image or video?

Name the soup and the bloom. Example: dense fog around [Subject], lamps becoming globes, figures appearing late. Give a short visibility distance and forbid crisp far detail.

Dense fog around [Subject], depth collapsing, lamps becoming globes, figures appearing late, horror or London grammar.

entries.title: Mist
entries.text:
Mist

Mist is a thinner water suspension than fog: pale layered air that still lets you read the next plane. Droplets are matter, but the veil is lyric, a morning or mountain breath rather than a wall.

Create this Mist

Narrative function

Ridges stack as paler copies of themselves. A horse is readable, then a second ridge, then a paler third.

Softer mystery than fog. Lyric, not monster.

Use it for dawn, river valleys, high cold air, a courtyard that should glow rather than vanish. It is the wrong tool when a killer should appear at two meters with no yard behind them: that is Fog.

It is the wrong tool when the paleness is only far, far away over desert: that is Atmospheric Haze. If you cannot see the subject at all, you overshot into fog.

If every plane is equally sharp, you have no mist.

How it works

Use a light density of droplets or a real inversion layer. Backlight the layers so each plane separates (aerial perspective at short-to-medium range).

Keep contrast on the near subject; let receding planes lift in value and lose saturation. Prompt: light mist around [Subject], softer than fog, morning or mountain breath, layers of pale air.

When to use it

Use it for a hunt at dawn, a mountain pass, a wet garden. Do not use it as horror soup, and do not fill an interior with it unless the windows are open on a cold morning.

Interiors with volume are often Smoke or haze juice, not mist.

Compared with similar shots

Fog hides. Atmospheric Haze is scattering over long distance, often without local wetness on skin.

Smoke has a source. Rain falls.

Mist hangs, layers, and remains see-through at working distance.

FogHide geography. Delay the reveal.

Atmospheric HazeShow kilometers, not just meters.

RainMake the air visible and the ground reflective.

In film

The Revenant uses morning and mountain moisture as stacked pale planes around bodies. Raise the Red Lantern lets courtyard air go milky without erasing architecture.

Use layered breath, not a white-out.

Prompt it

Light mist around [Subject], softer than fog, morning or mountain breath, layers of pale air. Name near-subject readability, paler far planes, and a backlight or low sun.

For video, slow drift of layers, no wall of white, no falling rain unless you add it.

Use in Image Generator

Light mist around [Subject], softer than fog, morning or mountain breath, layers of pale air.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Fog (too dense) or Atmospheric Haze (only the horizon pales). The tell: the hero vanishes, or only the skyline is pale while mid-ground is hard.

The fix: keep the subject readable, stack two or three paler planes, backlight the moisture.

Questions

What is Mist in film?

Mist is a light suspension of water droplets that layers the air without erasing the subject. It is thicker than clear air and thinner than fog.

Mist vs Fog

Fog collapses depth at short range and delays figures. Mist leaves the near ground readable and stacks pale planes. One is a wall; the other is breath.

When should I use Mist?

Use it for morning, mountains, and lyric distance at human scale. Do not use it when geography must disappear for a scare.

How do I prompt Mist for AI image or video?

Ask for layered pale air and a readable subject. Example: light mist around [Subject], softer than fog, morning or mountain breath. Specify backlight and forbid a white-out.

Melies is the AI filmmaking workspace. This Mist opens with the weather prompt loaded, so the atmosphere is in the photography.

Light mist around [Subject], softer than fog, morning or mountain breath, layers of pale air.

entries.title: Atmospheric Haze
entries.text:
Atmospheric Haze

hazefogsmokedustrainsnowsteam

Atmospheric haze is scattering over distance: far planes go paler and often cooler, so kilometers of air become the depth cue. The particles are too small to read as drops; the air is matter you measure in ridges, not in globes around a near lamp.

Create this Atmospheric Haze

Narrative function

A citadel sits in a paler key than the rider. The next cliff is paler still.

Show kilometers, not just meters. Depth is weather, not a second fog machine at the actor's feet.

Use it for desert, city, sea, any wide that must recede. It is the wrong tool when the next person should vanish at five meters (Fog) or when you want a shaft you can cut with a hand (Volumetric Light in a smoky room).

Haze is aerial perspective, not a local veil. If the foreground is milky, you hazed the lens, not the distance.

How it works

Keep the near ground relatively clean. Let successive planes lift in value, lose contrast, and often shift toward the sky color.

Dust, humidity, or pollution can be real; a graded aerial perspective can stand in if the physics hold. Hard sun through haze becomes a disk.

Prompt: atmospheric haze stacking distance around [Subject], aerial perspective, far planes paler, depth as weather.

When to use it

Use it on a ridge, a skyline, a valley, a megacity grid. Do not use it to hide a monster in a corridor.

If the scare is in the room, use fog, smoke, or darkness.

Compared with similar shots

Mist is local layered moisture at human distances. Fog is dense and near.

Volumetric Light is a beam made visible by particles, often indoors. Dust and Sand is wind-driven grit that attacks the near ground too.

Haze leaves the subject sharp and sends the world backward.

Volumetric LightAir has to be photographed, not just the subject.

MistSofter mystery than fog. Lyric, not monster.

RainMake the air visible and the ground reflective.

In film

Lawrence of Arabia lets desert distance go paler until armies are weather. Blade Runner 2049 stacks orange and pale planes so the city has kilometers.

Use successive paler ridges, not a fogged close-up.

Prompt it

Atmospheric haze stacking distance around [Subject], aerial perspective, far planes paler, depth as weather. Keep the near subject contrasty; name two or three receding planes.

For video, stable long-distance paleness, not swirling soup around the lens. No globes on a foreground practical unless you also have local fog.

Use in Image Generator

Atmospheric haze stacking distance around [Subject], aerial perspective, far planes paler, depth as weather.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Fog on the actor, or a low-contrast grade on every plane. The tell: the face is milky, or the far citadel is as sharp as the horse.

The fix: sharp near, paler far, several stacked distances, particles too small to resolve.

Questions

What is Atmospheric Haze in film?

Atmospheric haze is air scattering over long distance. Far planes go paler and lower in contrast while the near subject stays readable, so kilometers become visible.

Atmospheric Haze vs Mist

Mist is a local, often wet veil at walking distances. Haze is aerial perspective over kilometers. Mist can wet your coat; haze pales a mountain range.

When should I use Atmospheric Haze?

Use it when a wide must recede: desert, city, sea, valley. Do not use it to hide a figure in a room.

How do I prompt Atmospheric Haze for AI image or video?

Keep the subject sharp and pale the distance. Example: atmospheric haze stacking distance around [Subject], far planes paler. Name successive ridges or blocks of city, not a fog bank at the lens.

entries.title: Smoke
entries.text:
Smoke

hazefogdustrainsnowsteam

Smoke is combustion particles with a source, a direction, and enough density to turn a room's air into a volume the light can strike. Unlike weather fog, it has a chimney, a cigarette, a tire, or a battlefield; backlight carves it into shafts and swirls.

Create this Smoke

Narrative function

A practical lamp becomes a wedge through grey air. A drag on a cigarette writes a ribbon.

Photograph the air of a room. The walls were always there; now the air is too.

Use it when volume should be visible indoors or when a battle, a chimney, or a club must have a source. It is the wrong tool when the veil is weather with no fire (Fog, Mist).

It is the wrong tool when the white stuff rises off a manhole because water met cold air: that is Steam. Without a key or backlight, smoke is only a smell.

Front-filling a room with unlit smoke turns faces to mud.

How it works

Pick a source and a particle (cigarette, incense, oil, battlefield pot). Control air currents so ribbons have direction.

Light from the side or behind so the volume renders; use a hard beam if you want shafts (Volumetric Light). Keep some clean path to the face.

Prompt: smoke around [Subject], cigarette, chimney, or battle, shafts of light catching it, volume in the room.

When to use it

Use it for apartments, temples, engine rooms, aftermath. Do not use it as a default 'atmosphere' pass on a sunny kitchen.

If the beat is stillness in a closed parlor, Dust Motes in a shaft may be enough.

Compared with similar shots

Atmospheric Haze in the distance is aerial perspective. A hazer used to fill a stage is a cousin of smoke but without a story source; still light it as volume.

Fog is wet weather. Steam is water vapor from heat, white, rising, condensing.

Dust Motes are discrete specks in a beam, not a ribbon.

Atmospheric HazeShow kilometers, not just meters.

Volumetric LightAir has to be photographed, not just the subject.

RainMake the air visible and the ground reflective.

In film

In the Mood for Love lets cigarette ribbons occupy cramped rooms. Blade Runner fills interiors so shafts and practicals have air to hit.

Apocalypse Now makes battle and jungle air into volume. Give smoke a source and a light, not a generic grey.

Prompt it

Smoke around [Subject], cigarette, chimney, or battle, shafts of light catching it, volume in the room. Name the source, the backlight or side key, and the direction of the ribbon.

For video, swirling volume, not a static fog plate, and a still-readable face.

Use in Image Generator

Smoke around [Subject], cigarette, chimney, or battle, shafts of light catching it, volume in the room.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Fog (no source) or unlit fill that dirties skin. The tell: no chimney or cigarette, lamps without shafts, a muddy key.

The fix: a visible source, side or back light, a clean path to the eyes.

Questions

What is Smoke in film?

Smoke is airborne combustion particles from a source, dense enough that light can carve the room's air into volume. It has direction, swirls, and a reason to exist.

Smoke vs Atmospheric Haze

Haze pales distant planes over kilometers. Smoke occupies a room or a battlefield and needs a source and a sculpting light. One is distance; the other is volume you could walk through.

When should I use Smoke?

Use it to photograph a room's air, a chimney, a cigarette, a battle. Do not use it as weather, and do not fill a face with unlit particles.

How do I prompt Smoke for AI image or video?

Name source and lighting. Example: smoke around [Subject], cigarette, chimney, or battle, shafts of light catching it. Demand a readable face and visible volume, not a grey grade.

entries.title: Dust Motes
entries.text:
Dust Motes

Dust motes are discrete particles hanging in a shaft of light, slow enough to read as time in still air. They are matter you can almost count; they live in the beam, not as a veil across the whole room.

Create this Dust Motes

Narrative function

A window cuts a wedge through a closed parlor. Specks drift, rise, fall.

Stillness that is still alive. The room has been shut; time is visible because the air has a population.

Use it when quiet should not be empty: a church, a bedroom, a barn in late sun. It is the wrong tool when the air is a ribbon from a cigarette (Smoke) or a soup that hides the far wall (Fog).

It is the wrong tool when the particles are on fire (Sparks and Embers). If the whole room is milky, you filled it.

Motes need a dark surround and a hard beam.

How it works

Create a shaft (window, slats, a cut HMI) and keep off-beam air darker. Introduce fine particles (real dust, atmosphere in small amounts).

Backlight or sidelight the beam; motes are seen by scatter toward camera. Slow movement: convection, not wind.

Prompt: dust motes hanging in a shaft of light around [Subject], slow particles, a room that has been closed, time made visible.

When to use it

Use it for a pause, a prayer, a house that remembers. Do not use it in a gale or a nightclub wash.

If the camera is racing, motes become streaks or noise. Pair with Slow Motion only if you want to inventory the specks.

Compared with similar shots

Volumetric Light is the shaft; dust motes are the countable inhabitants of that shaft. Smoke is a continuous volume.

Sparks and Embers are incandescent and short-lived. Atmospheric Haze pales the far plane.

Motes are slow, discrete, and local to the beam.

Volumetric LightAir has to be photographed, not just the subject.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

RainMake the air visible and the ground reflective.

In film

The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford lets window light populate air so interiors feel timed. The Tree of Life hangs specks in domestic and cosmic shafts.

Use beam plus specks, not a dusty grade on a flatly lit room.

Prompt it

Dust motes hanging in a shaft of light around [Subject], slow particles, a room that has been closed, time made visible. Name the window or slat, the dark surround, and that particles are discrete, not a fog fill.

For video, slow drift inside the beam only.

Use in Image Generator

Dust motes hanging in a shaft of light around [Subject], slow particles, a room that has been closed, time made visible.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Smoke fill or Volumetric Light with no specks. The tell: milky room, no shaft, or sparks.

The fix: a hard beam, dark off-beam, countable slow particles, backlight.

Questions

What is Dust Motes in film?

Dust motes are individual particles visible in a shaft of light. They make still air readable as matter and time, without turning the whole room into fog.

Dust Motes vs Volumetric Light

Volumetric light is the visible beam. Dust motes are the specks inside it. You can have a shaft with smooth haze, or a shaft with countable motes; the mote look insists on the specks.

When should I use Dust Motes?

Use them when stillness should still be alive: closed rooms, late sun, churches. Do not fill the entire volume, and do not substitute fire sparks.

How do I prompt Dust Motes for AI image or video?

Put specks in a shaft, not soup in a room. Example: dust motes hanging in a shaft of light around [Subject], slow particles, a room that has been closed. Dark surround, backlight, no fog fill.

entries.title: Steam
entries.text:
Steam

hazefogsmokedustrainsnow

Steam is water vapor released where heat meets colder air: trains, manholes, showers, a white veil that rises and thins. It is wet matter, not combustion; it billows, condenses on lens and wool, and has a thermal source.

Create this Steam

Narrative function

A locomotive writes a column that the platform wind tears. A manhole breathes.

A shower erases a body in white. Heat meeting cold air.

Industrial or intimate, the physics are the same. Use it when the source is hot water or hot metal in cold space.

It is the wrong tool when the cloud is burning (Smoke) or hanging as weather (Fog). Smoke can sink and stain; steam wants to rise and vanish.

If the white cloud has no grate, kettle, train, or shower, you have fog in a trench coat.

How it works

Show the source (stack, manhole, shower head, kettle). Let the vapor rise and shear in wind.

Backlight for a white, translucent volume; it should feel wetter and brighter than smoke. Condensation on glass and wool helps.

Prompt: steam billowing around [Subject], trains, manholes, showers, a white veil, industrial or intimate heat.

When to use it

Use it on a winter platform, a night street grate, a bathroom, a factory press. Do not use it as generic alley 'atmosphere' with no heat.

If the alley is burning, use smoke. If the alley is only wet and cold, use fog or rain.

Compared with similar shots

Smoke is combustion, often grey or colored, with a fire source. Fog is ambient water droplets without a hot origin.

Atmospheric Haze is distant scatter. Steam is a thermal event: white, rising, local to a grate, stack, or shower.

SmokePhotograph the air of a room.

FogHide geography. Delay the reveal.

RainMake the air visible and the ground reflective.

In film

Winter station grammar in thrillers leans on locomotive steam as moving architecture. The Untouchables uses train steam as a white, violent veil.

Drive lets night streets breathe from grates. Spirited Away treats bathhouse steam as a wet interior weather.

Show the heat, not a smoke bomb.

Prompt it

Steam billowing around [Subject], trains, manholes, showers, a white veil, industrial or intimate heat. Name the hot source, the cold air, backlight, and rise.

For video, billows that shear and thin, condensation, no grey cigarette ribbons unless you also have smoke.

Use in Image Generator

Steam billowing around [Subject], trains, manholes, showers, a white veil, industrial or intimate heat.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Smoke (wrong color, wrong source) or Fog (no rise from heat). The tell: a grey cloud sitting still with no grate or stack.

The fix: a thermal source, white translucent rise, backlight, wind shear.

Questions

What is Steam in film?

Steam is water vapor from heat meeting colder air. It billows from trains, manholes, showers, and kettles: a white, wet, rising veil with a thermal source.

Steam vs Smoke

Smoke is combustion particles and can hang, stain, and go grey. Steam is wet vapor, brighter, rising, tied to heat and cold air. One burns; the other boils.

When should I use Steam?

Use it when heat and cold air are in the scene: platforms, grates, baths, presses. Do not use it as a generic alley cloud with no source.

How do I prompt Steam for AI image or video?

Name the hot source and the white rise. Example: steam billowing around [Subject], trains, manholes, showers, a white veil. Backlight it and keep it wetter than smoke.

Melies is the AI filmmaking workspace. This Steam opens with the weather prompt loaded, so the atmosphere is in the photography.

entries.title: Snow
entries.text:
Snow

hazefogsmokedustrainsteam

Snow is ice falling and settling: large flakes in backlight, a muffled world, tracks that record who passed. The air holds crystals you can size; the ground accumulates; contrast goes soft because the world has been covered.

Create this Snow

Narrative function

Flakes cross a sodium lamp like slow sparks that do not burn. Shoulders collect white.

Footsteps write the path. Hush the world.

Silence becomes visible as reduced contrast and falling matter. Use it when winter must occupy both air and ground.

It is the wrong tool when you only need pale air without accumulation (Mist). It is the wrong tool when the falling matter is liquid (Rain).

Rain wets and mirrors; snow blankets and records tracks. Tiny fast specks against a day sky read as video noise.

Size the flakes and backlight them.

How it works

Put flakes in the air (practical or digital) large enough to read, and light them from behind or the side. Let accumulation sit on wool, hair, rails, and ground.

Keep a dark background for flakes to separate, or accept a white-on-white hush. Wind decides drift versus fall.

Prompt: falling snow around [Subject], large flakes in backlight, muffled world, tracks, winter silence you can see.

When to use it

Use it for a platform wait, a hunt, a small-town crime, a night street that should go quiet. Do not use it as white rain that never settles.

If shoulders stay dry and the pavement is only wet, you shot rain.

Compared with similar shots

Rain streaks and mirrors. Mist hangs and does not accumulate as a blanket.

Blue Hour is a sky condition that often pairs with snow but is not weather. Dust Motes are indoor specks in a shaft.

Snow falls, lands, and stays.

MistSofter mystery than fog. Lyric, not monster.

Blue HourDay is gone but the sky still works.

RainMake the air visible and the ground reflective.

In film

Fargo lets snow be ground, air, and isolation. Let the Right One In uses falling flakes and muffled suburbs.

The Revenant puts bodies into falling and settled winter. Use accumulation and backlight, not a noise overlay.

Prompt it

Falling snow around [Subject], large flakes in backlight, muffled world, tracks, winter silence you can see. Name flake size, a lamp or sun behind them, accumulation on shoulders and ground, and tracks if anyone has walked.

For video, fall plus settle; no dry coats, no rain streaks.

Use in Image Generator

Falling snow around [Subject], large flakes in backlight, muffled world, tracks, winter silence you can see.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Rain tinted white, or grain called snow. The tell: wet mirrors, no accumulation, specks too small to size.

The fix: large backlit flakes, settled white on surfaces, tracks, a hush in contrast.

Questions

What is Snow in film?

Snow is ice in the air and on the ground: backlit flakes, accumulation, tracks, a quieter contrast. It occupies volume and records passage.

Snow vs Rain

Rain is liquid: streaks, splashes, mirrors. Snow is crystal: drift, settle, blanket. If the street specularizes and coats stay dark, you are still in rain.

When should I use Snow?

Use it when winter should hush the world and leave tracks. Do not use it as white rain, and do not omit accumulation.

How do I prompt Snow for AI image or video?

Specify large backlit flakes and settled white. Example: falling snow around [Subject], large flakes in backlight, muffled world, tracks. Demand accumulation on wool and ground.

entries.title: Wet-Down
entries.text:
Wet-Down

A wet-down sprays pavement, asphalt, and cars so night lights double themselves in reflection, often with no rain in the air. The street is the effect; water is a surface treatment, not weather.

Create this Wet-Down

Narrative function

Sodium, neon, a traffic headlamp: each finds a second copy on blacktop. Night exteriors that must sparkle.

Studio crews invented this because dry asphalt eats light. The trick is the shine, not the storm.

Use it when a night street, alley, or overpass must specularize practicals. It is the wrong tool when you need falling streaks and umbrellas as percussion: add Rain.

It is the wrong tool when the color should come only from tubes on walls with a dry floor: that is Neon Practicals without a mirror. If the air is full of drops, you have rain (usually on top of a wet-down).

If the air is empty and the ground is a black mirror, you have the wet-down alone.

How it works

Hose or rain-bar the travel path until it sheets. Place practicals (sodium, neon, shop windows) so their reflections fall in frame.

Keep the camera low enough to catch the mirror, or lose it. No need for backlight in the air unless rain is also falling.

Prompt: wet-down streets around [Subject], pavement sprayed for night, double the lights by reflection.

When to use it

Use it for night driving, a sidewalk wait, a neon block. Do not soak a dusty noon street unless the story has just rained.

A wet-down in hard sun can look like a spill, not night grammar.

Compared with similar shots

Rain puts drops in the optical path. Neon Practicals is the source color; wet-down is how that color doubles on the ground.

Fog blooms lamps in air. Wet-down blooms them on the floor.

Atmospheric Haze does not spec the asphalt.

RainMake the air visible and the ground reflective.

Neon PracticalsThe city is the lighting department.

FogHide geography. Delay the reveal.

In film

Drive and Collateral make Los Angeles nights out of wet asphalt and practicals. Who Framed Roger Rabbit's night streets use the same studio-wet logic so lamps have copies.

Use the mirror, not a copied car.

Prompt it

Wet-down streets around [Subject], pavement sprayed for night, double the lights by reflection. Name the practicals, the sheeting water on asphalt, and empty air unless rain is also requested.

For video, moving reflections, tire tracks in water, no falling streaks if you do not want rain.

Use in Image Generator

Wet-down streets around [Subject], pavement sprayed for night, double the lights by reflection, studio-night trick made beautiful.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Rain (streaks in air) or a glossy grade on dry pavement. The tell: drops around lamps, or no reflections despite 'wet streets.' The fix: sheet the ground, place lights that can reflect, keep air empty if rain is not the job.

Questions

What is Wet-Down in film?

A wet-down is a sprayed street or surface that turns night practicals into reflections. It is a ground treatment. Rain is optional.

Wet-Down vs Rain

Rain is weather in the air. Wet-down is water on the ground so lights double. Night work often uses both; they are not the same request.

When should I use Wet-Down?

Use it when a night exterior must sparkle from the pavement. Do not use it as a substitute for falling rain, and do not soak a dry noon scene without a story reason.

How do I prompt Wet-Down for AI image or video?

Ask for sprayed pavement and reflected practicals. Example: wet-down streets around [Subject], pavement sprayed for night, double the lights by reflection. Specify empty air if you do not want rain.

entries.title: Sparks and Embers
entries.text:
Sparks and Embers

Sparks and embers are incandescent particles thrown by welding, fire, grinding, or a cigarette: orange weather with short trajectories. They are burning matter; backlight is optional because they are their own small keys.

Create this Sparks and Embers

Narrative function

A welder writes a fountain. A collapsing floor throws embers that hang, then die.

Industry or apocalypse in the air. Unlike dust, these specks have temperature and a brief life.

Use it when the air should be dangerous or industrial: a foundry, a burning street, a cigarette in a dark booth (embers, not a fountain). It is the wrong tool when the specks are cold (Dust Motes, Snow).

It is the wrong tool when the glow is only a warm key on a face with no particles: that is Candlelight or firelight without weather. If the particles are large, slow, and white, you probably asked for snow.

If they never fall, you asked for hanging dust.

How it works

Give them a source (welder, angle grinder, timber, cigarette). Let gravity and heat dictate: sparks drop and bounce; embers can loft and drift.

Expose for the particle without losing the face entirely, or accept silhouettes. A dark surround makes them read.

Prompt: sparks or embers around [Subject], welding, fire, cigarettes, orange particles as weather.

When to use it

Use it for a night burn, a factory, a ruined city, a match. Do not sprinkle orange specks on a pastoral wide with no fire.

Particles need a reason.

Compared with similar shots

Candlelight is a warm, flickering key. Sparks are the particles.

Volumetric Light is a shaft; sparks can cross it but are not the shaft. Dust Motes are cold and slow in a beam.

Snow is cold and accumulates. Sparks die in the air.

CandlelightPeriod night or ritual.

Volumetric LightAir has to be photographed, not just the subject.

RainMake the air visible and the ground reflective.

In film

Blade Runner 2049 throws orange particles as industrial weather. The Dark Knight Rises uses fire and debris as airborne specks in night action.

Use source plus trajectory, not a spark overlay on a clean street.

Prompt it

Sparks or embers around [Subject], welding, fire, cigarettes, orange particles as weather. Name the source, color (white-orange to dull red), trajectory (fountain versus lofted drift), and a dark surround.

For video, short-lived particles with gravity; no snow, no cigarette smoke unless you also want smoke.

Use in Image Generator

Sparks or embers around [Subject], welding, fire, cigarettes, orange particles as weather.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Dust Motes tinted orange, or Snow. The tell: specks hang forever, accumulate on the ground as white, or have no welder or fire.

The fix: a hot source, brief trajectories, self-luminous particles, dark air.

Questions

What is Sparks and Embers in film?

Sparks and embers are burning particles in the air, thrown by welding, fire, or a cigarette. They light themselves, follow short trajectories, and die.

Sparks and Embers vs Dust Motes

Dust motes are cold specks in a shaft of light. Sparks are incandescent and come from a hot source. One is time in a closed room; the other is industry or fire.

When should I use Sparks and Embers?

Use them when the air should carry heat: welding, collapse, a cigarette coal. Do not sprinkle orange dots on a scene with no fire.

How do I prompt Sparks and Embers for AI image or video?

Name the hot source and the trajectories. Example: sparks or embers around [Subject], welding, fire, cigarettes, orange particles as weather. Dark surround, gravity, no snow.

entries.title: Dust and Sand
entries.text:
Dust and Sand

Dust and sand as weather is mineral grit driven by wind until the sun is a dull coin and figures become silhouettes. The land attacks: particles occupy near air, sting highlights, and erase the horizon that Atmospheric Haze would only pale.

Create this Dust and Sand

Narrative function

A rider is a cutout. The sun is a disk you can look at.

Grit crawls across metal and teeth. This is not a poetic far ridge.

This is the ground in the lungs. Use it when the environment is an antagonist: border desert, convoy, siege.

It is the wrong tool when you only need paler mountains behind a sharp hero (Atmospheric Haze). It is the wrong tool when the particles hang in a quiet indoor shaft (Dust Motes).

Hard Light through a storm becomes a brown disk; do not keep a crisp white sun and a clean face unless the storm is still on the way.

How it works

Fill near and mid air with wind-driven particulates (fuller's earth, practical sand, or digital grit) so contrast collapses at working distance. Keep a strong directional wind.

Backlight or sun-through-dust to silhouette. Let highlights on skin and vehicles pick up specks.

Prompt: dust or sandstorm wrapping [Subject], sun as a dull coin, silhouettes, grit in the highlights.

When to use it

Use it for an ambush, a crossing, a road that should be unsurvivable. Do not use it as a warm grade on a calm dune.

If flags hang limp and pores are clean, there is no storm.

Compared with similar shots

Atmospheric Haze is calm aerial perspective over kilometers, subject still sharp. Fog is water, grey-white, little wind required.

Smoke has a fire source. Hard Light is the sun's character; in a storm that sun is filtered.

Dust-storm is mineral, windy, and near.

Atmospheric HazeShow kilometers, not just meters.

Hard LightGrit, noon sun, or interrogation.

RainMake the air visible and the ground reflective.

In film

Sicario lets desert particulate erase edges and turn daylight hostile. Mad Max: Fury Road drives through walls of grit and sun as a coin.

Lawrence of Arabia also uses blowing sand as an attack, not only distant haze. Use wind and near opacity, not a tan LUT.

Prompt it

Dust or sandstorm wrapping [Subject], sun as a dull coin, silhouettes, grit in the highlights. Name wind direction, reduced visibility, and dirty speculars on skin and metal.

For video, horizontal grit, flapping cloth, no calm air, no sharp far town unless it is a brief hole in the storm.

Use in Image Generator

Dust or sandstorm wrapping [Subject], sun as a dull coin, silhouettes, grit in the highlights, Sicario weather.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is Atmospheric Haze (sharp rider, paler citadel) or a brown grade. The tell: clean pores, limp flags, a white sun, crisp horizon.

The fix: wind, near-air grit, silhouettes, a dull solar disk, specks on highlights.

Questions

What is Dust and Sand in film?

Dust and sand as a storm is wind-driven mineral in the air, dense enough to silhouette figures and turn the sun into a dull coin. The land occupies the near optical path.

Dust and Sand vs Atmospheric Haze

Haze pales far planes and leaves the subject sharp. A dust storm attacks the near ground, reduces visibility, and needs wind. One is distance; the other is an assault.

When should I use Dust and Sand?

Use it when the land should attack: crossings, convoys, sieges. Do not use it as a warm filter on a still desert portrait.

How do I prompt Dust and Sand for AI image or video?

Ask for wind-driven grit and a dull sun. Example: dust or sandstorm wrapping [Subject], sun as a dull coin, silhouettes, grit in the highlights. Demand dirty air at working distance.

entries.title: Underwater
entries.text:
Underwater

Underwater cinematography leaves air: the camera is in water, so caustics, buoyancy, and a missing horizon rewrite every edge. The medium is the matter; particles are silt and bubbles, and bodies move as if the world had gone slow without a slow-motion shutter.

Volume

Create this Underwater

Narrative function

Hair and cloth delay. Light arrives as moving lattice from a surface that is now a ceiling.

There is no standing horizon, only up toward silver and down toward dark. Leave air.

Use it when the scene is actually submerged: a pool, a sea, a tank, a flood. It is the wrong tool when you only want grace: dry Slow Motion with a blue grade is a lie, and it shows in hair that still falls at air speed.

It is the wrong tool when the story is on the swell with a sky: that is Ocean. Color dies with depth (reds first).

If the red dress is still loud at ten meters, you stayed in air.

How it works

Put the lens in a housing in water (or a convincing tank). Expose for caustics from the real sun or a hard source through the surface.

Let bubbles and silt backlight. Wardrobe and hair must float.

Camera moves fight drag; they read slower. Prompt: underwater of [Subject], caustics, muffled space, hair and cloth in slow water, a world without horizon.

When to use it

Use it for a dive, a drowning, a creature, a flooded corridor. Do not use it as a look for a dry bedroom.

If you need the surface and the sky, shoot ocean, then go under for a beat if the story dives.

Compared with similar shots

Ocean is the surface world: swell, horizon, salt light. Atmospheric Haze is air scatter.

Slow Motion is a frame-rate choice that often accompanies underwater but is not the medium. Underwater is a different optical path: refraction, caustics, buoyancy, no air horizon.

Atmospheric HazeShow kilometers, not just meters.

Slow MotionA second contains a scene.

RainMake the air visible and the ground reflective.

In film

The Big Blue lives in the medium, not in a tint. The Shape of Water makes tanks and canals a second gravity.

Thunderball proved action can be staged as true submerged geography. Use caustics and float, not a teal LUT on a dry actor.

Prompt it

Underwater of [Subject], caustics, muffled space, hair and cloth in slow water, a world without horizon. Name depth, the surface as ceiling or absence, floating wardrobe, silt or bubbles in backlight.

For video, buoyancy and drag; no air-speed hair, no standing horizon unless looking up at the underside of the surface.

Use in Image Generator

Underwater of [Subject], caustics, muffled space, hair and cloth in slow water, a world without horizon.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a blue grade in air, or Ocean from a boat. The tell: cloth hangs, hair falls, a skyline, no caustics.

The fix: submerge the camera, float the fabrics, add caustics and backlit silt, kill the air horizon.

Questions

What is Underwater in film?

Underwater work puts camera and subject in water, so caustics, buoyancy, particles, and a missing air horizon rewrite the frame. The medium is the atmosphere.

Underwater vs Ocean

Ocean is the surface: swell, sky, a horizon that can kill you. Underwater leaves that sky and treats the surface as a ceiling. One is a seascape; the other is a different world.

When should I use Underwater?

Use it when the scene is submerged. Do not use a blue grade or slow motion in air as a substitute, and do not call a boat horizon underwater.

How do I prompt Underwater for AI image or video?

Demand caustics, floating cloth, and no air horizon. Example: underwater of [Subject], caustics, muffled space, hair and cloth in slow water. Specify silt or bubbles in backlight.

entries.title: Ocean
entries.text:
Ocean

Ocean cinematography treats the sea as the other actor: swell, a horizon, salt light, a person against water that does not care. The atmosphere is spray, haze over distance, and a moving floor; the camera is in air, on a hull, or on rocks, not yet in the lung of the sea.

Volume

Create this Ocean

Narrative function

A mole, a boat, a body: small. The horizon is a line that can kill you.

Swell has a period. Salt in backlight is weather.

The sea is the other actor. Use it for exile, work, awe, war at the rail.

It is the wrong tool when you have left the surface (Underwater). It is the wrong tool when the water is a still lake used as silk behind a posed figure.

If there is no swell and no scale, it is not ocean. A bathtub, a pool, a harbor with no fetch: different jobs.

Name the swell.

How it works

Shoot wide enough for scale. Put real swell in the frame (period, whitecaps or long rollers).

Backlight spray. Let far water go paler with Atmospheric Haze.

Keep the human or boat small unless the story is a face against a rail. Practical water on lens is allowed; fake silk water is not.

Prompt: ocean world of [Subject], swell, horizon, salt light, a person against water that does not care.

When to use it

Use it when the sea must act: a crossing, a lighthouse rock, a mole under fire, a diver's surface world. Do not use it as a backdrop for fashion on calm glass.

If the camera goes under, switch techniques.

Compared with similar shots

Underwater submerges the lens. Atmospheric Haze is the aerial perspective over the water, a modifier, not the whole job.

Rain can lash a surface but is not swell. Ocean is surface gravity, horizon, and scale.

A wet street is not an ocean.

UnderwaterLeave air.

Atmospheric HazeShow kilometers, not just meters.

RainMake the air visible and the ground reflective.

In film

The Big Blue treats the surface as a workplace and a temptation. The Lighthouse puts two men against water and rock with no kindness in the horizon.

Dunkirk uses mole, hull, and swell as hostile architecture. Show weight and weather, not a stock seascape.

Prompt it

Ocean world of [Subject], swell, horizon, salt light, a person against water that does not care. Name sea state, scale (small figure or small boat), backlight on spray, and a hard horizon.

For video, real period in the swell, not a looping texture. Do not make the water a silk backdrop.

Use in Image Generator

Ocean world of [Subject], swell, horizon, salt light, a person against water that does not care.

What usually goes wrong

The usual wrong cousin is a calm stock seascape or Underwater caustics on a dry beach. The tell: no swell, a posed model large in frame, glass-smooth water, no spray.

The fix: scale the human down, give the sea a period, backlight salt, keep the horizon honest.

Questions

What is Ocean in film?

Ocean work puts a person or boat against real swell and a horizon, with salt light and spray in the air. The sea is an actor, not a backdrop.

Ocean vs Underwater

Ocean is the surface world: sky, swell, horizon. Underwater submerges the camera and loses that horizon. One is weather and scale; the other is a different medium.

When should I use Ocean?

Use it when the sea must act on a body, a boat, or a rock. Do not use a still lake or a pool, and do not stay in ocean grammar once the lens has left the air.

How do I prompt Ocean for AI image or video?

Name swell, horizon, and scale. Example: ocean world of [Subject], swell, horizon, salt light, a person against water that does not care. Demand period in the waves and backlight on spray.
